name: Lake Chad Basin insurgency outside Nigeria (Cameroon Far North, Chad Lac, Niger Diffa)
started: 2014-01-01 (approximate: Boko Haram spillover into Cameroon and Chad from 2014)
summary: Boko Haram and ISWAP raid across Nigeria's borders into Cameroon's Far North, Chad's Lake Chad islands and Niger's Diffa region, mixing attacks on army posts with kidnapping and looting of villages. Cameroon recorded 425 militant-linked deaths in 2025 (Africa Center), and Boko Haram killed 23 Chadian soldiers on Barka Tolorom island in May 2026. The theatre matters because the lake's islands and marshes are the shared rear base for both jihadist factions.

sides.name: Lake Chad states
backers: United States (exploring expanded cooperation with Cameroon; AFRICOM met President Biya in May 2026)

sides.name: Jihadist groups
members: Boko Haram (JAS), including Bakura Doro's Lake Chad faction

background: The insurgency spilled out of northeast Nigeria from 2014, drawing Cameroon, Chad and Niger into the Multinational Joint Task Force. Lake Chad's shrinking, island-studded basin is ideal terrain for small boats and hideouts, and the fishing and smuggling economy funds ISWAP. Boko Haram's Bakura Doro faction is based on the lake islands and has also fought ISWAP there.

In Cameroon the Far North (Mayo-Sava, Mayo-Tsanaga, Logone-et-Chari) sees frequent raids, kidnappings for ransom and attacks on vigilance committees. Why it matters: the four states' cooperation has frayed (Niger's junta has cooled on Western partners) while the US is exploring new security ties with Cameroon.
year: Violence continued at a lower but steady level. In Chad, Boko Haram attacked a garrison on Barka Tolorom island on 4 May 2026, killing 23 soldiers. In Cameroon's Far North, insurgents targeted civilians, looted and kidnapped for ransom; June 2026 recorded the most violence in Mayo-Tsanaga since July 2025, and the US explored expanded military cooperation after an AFRICOM meeting with President Biya in May and an envoy visit in June (ACLED). In Niger's Diffa region, a separate rebel group, the Patriotic Liberation Movement for Justice, sabotaged the Niger-Benin oil pipeline near Agadem with an IED on 16 Nov 2025 and followed up with IEDs on patrols (ACLED). Cameroon's disputed October 2025 election, with protests in Garoua and Maroua in the north, added political stress.
situation: As of late October 2026 the jihadist threat in the three countries is chronic rather than escalating: small-unit raids, kidnappings and periodic attacks on island garrisons. Chad is also stretched by Sudan war spillover on its eastern border, and Cameroon by the Anglophone conflict.
technical: Barka Tolorom (Chad) island garrison attack on 4 May 2026 killed 23 soldiers, showing JAS's continued capacity for boat-borne assaults on the lake (Wikipedia, 2026 in Chad).
Cameroon's Far North: insurgents kidnap for ransom and loot; Mayo-Tsanaga saw its most violence since July 2025 in June 2026 (ACLED).
ISWAP foreign fighters are reported in Niger's Bosso area near the lake (HumAngle).

Niger's Diffa region also hosts non-jihadist rebels: the Patriotic Liberation Movement for Justice IED attack on the Niger-Benin pipeline near Agadem (16 Nov 2025), and an IED on a vehicle carrying Chinese civilians between Agadem and Koulele (ACLED).
Chad's army is also fighting Sudan spillover: RSF cross-border attack on Birak garrison (15 Jan 2026, 7 soldiers killed) and a drone strike on Tine (18 Mar 2026, 17 killed) (Wikipedia, 2026 in Chad).
Cameroon recorded 425 militant-linked deaths in 2025, a decline from earlier years (Africa Center).
casualties: Africa Center (2025): Cameroon 425 militant Islamist-linked deaths (declining). Chad: 23 soldiers killed at Barka Tolorom (May 2026). No consolidated 12-month total for Chad or Niger's Diffa found.

timeline.event: Cameroon's Constitutional Council declares Biya re-elected; protests in Douala, Garoua and Maroua (at least 48 killed nationally, ACLED).
Pipeline sabotaged near Agadem, Diffa region, Niger, by the Patriotic Liberation Movement for Justice.
Boko Haram attack on Barka Tolorom island garrison in Chad kills 23 soldiers.
June ends as the most violent month in Mayo-Tsanaga, Cameroon, since July 2025.

outlook: Watch the dry season (lake levels fall and mobility rises), ISWAP-JAS fighting on the islands, the shape of any new US-Cameroon security cooperation, and whether Chad's attention is diverted further by the Sudan war.
